shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: verified-capture (Desktop)

children.name: Demo title
children.text: A valid checksum cannot identify the author

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Inspect four invented notes. A replacement can pass every integrity check while its producing build remains unknown.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: Repacked replacement: valid note. Producing build: unknown. Its checksum agrees with its replacement payload, so integrity passes without proving origin.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Invented in-memory specimens, not the R5 capture format or captured firmware. No files are read or uploaded.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: Original: valid. Truncated: length mismatch. Changed byte: CRC mismatch. Repacked replacement: valid. The producing build is unknown for all four specimens.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: finding-audio (Mobile)

children.name: Demo title
children.text: A busy stream can repeat itself

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Compare neighboring values, then compare matching positions. Drop a word to see why the error counter matters.

children.name: error-note
children.text: Error count: 0 to 0 / the frame repeats

children.name: Demo result
children.text: 4 adjacent changes. The counter rises although the complete frame repeats unchanged.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Invented four-position frames. These values are not captured samples or named physical channels.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: The repeated frame [0, 7, 7, 0] produces four adjacent changes but zero same-position changes. A changed error count makes the shifted comparison invalid.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: ram-loader (Desktop)

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Inspect a stage of the fictional handoff, then ask whether the normal writer may use the same buffer.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: RAM mode owns the buffer, including after sealing. A simultaneous normal writer request is rejected.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Ownership model only. It receives no program and performs no execution, reset or device operation.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: RAM admission closes the normal writer route. Sealing retains RAM ownership. A recorded fresh return restores the writer. Cancellation requires a reset before writer ownership can return.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: first-change (Mobile)

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Choose a fictional record change. Check its length, fixed terminator position and surrounding bytes at their original offsets.

children.name: scope
children.text: Preset comparisons only / no firmware input

children.name: Demo result
children.text: Fictional record: 15 bytes before, 15 after. Length preserved; fixed terminator position preserved; surrounding bytes at original offsets preserved. All three checks pass.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Fixed, invented in-memory records. This comparison accepts no files and cannot modify or install firmware.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: A twelve-character replacement preserves the record length, terminator position and surrounding bytes. An extra byte changes the length and moves both the terminator and trailing guard, failing all three checks. A changed terminator or surrounding byte fails its own check.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: synth-design (Desktop)

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Edit, store or initialize the fictional patch. Confirm or cancel, then check the patch name, edited marker and held take.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: Ready to edit. Patch: Example patch, edited. Held take: phrase-1, unchanged. This is a fictional interface state, not installed synth behavior.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Interface model only. A retained take is an explicit rule of this exercise, not a demonstrated SP recording or storage feature.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: Cancel preserves the current patch name and edited state. Initialize produces Init, clean. Store produces My patch, clean. All three outcomes retain the model’s phrase-1 take.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: named-inputs (Mobile)

children.name: Demo title
children.text: A new event can still look unchanged

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Scrub the first 60 counts of this invented return sweep. Watch the raw reading, event anchor and visible outputs separately.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: Sample 7 of 7: raw 3940, event anchor 3940, 1% and 1 pixel. 3 events have passed the 16-count gate.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Invented readings reproduce the existing exercise’s software layers. No shaft angle, physical timing or calibrated control response is represented.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: With a 16-count gate, the sweep emits 3984 with 0% and 0 pixels, 3968 with 0% and 1 pixel, then 3940 with 1% and 1 pixel. A 64-count gate emits nothing during this 60-count return.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: partial-update (Desktop)

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Change the cost of each fictional job. Compare a shared allowance with a fresh, bounded allowance per job.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: The shared allowance completes 2 of three jobs; a separate ten-unit allowance completes all three. Each inner operation still has a finite bound.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Invented work units, not flash timing or device progress. Cleanup has its own bounded allowance.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: Three jobs costing four units each exhaust a shared allowance of ten after two jobs. Ten units per job admits all three. A job costing eleven is rejected; successful cleanup does not erase that failure.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: usb-updates (Desktop)

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Choose an evidence checkpoint. Watch memory, storage and the running program change separately.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: The example target has a matching fresh identity after the storage and status checks.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Illustrative evidence model. Example identities and timing are invented; no USB operation occurs.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: RAM verification proves receipt. Storage readback proves the checked storage result. A matching fresh identity is still needed to establish a new boot.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: original-boot (Mobile)

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Compare the initial observation with SHIFT press and release. The changing counters describe different parts of the same received packet.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: After SHIFT release: 2 added packets, 8 added received bytes and 8 added interrupt entries. Transmit failures remain 0; framing errors remain 1. This does not establish pad input or measured timing.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Schematic comparison of the R7 photographs. Counts above the rule are deltas from the initial observation; movement and timing are illustrative.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: Each SHIFT edge added one packet, four received bytes and four interrupt-handler entries. Across initial, press and release observations, transmit failures stayed at zero and the framing-error count stayed at one.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: keeping-the-updater (Mobile)

children.name: Demo title
children.text: The writer lives inside a package

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Replace the application, then inspect the startup path. The outgoing writer does not transfer itself into the new package.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: The tested wrapped application retains B1. Its later fresh writer startup was checked separately from the A1 screen.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Component-ownership diagram of the recorded packages. This is not a boot or installation procedure.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: R16B contains its USB writer. R3 replaces that application and has no R16B writer. The tested A1 + B1 package includes separate application and writer paths within APP1.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: original-sdk (Desktop)

children.name: Demo title
children.text: Watch the bytes stay inside their contract

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Choose samples and a destination capacity. Follow one value through clipping and little-endian output.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: Four signed values need eight bytes. The selected input -40000 clips to -32768; its low byte is written first. Guard cells remain unchanged.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Generic signed 16-bit model with invented samples. These eight bytes are not an SP transmit-frame definition.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: The samples -40000, -1, 1 and 40000 produce 00 80 ff ff 01 00 ff 7f after clipping. Insufficient capacity leaves every sentinel byte unchanged.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: mapping-controls (Desktop)

children.name: Demo title
children.text: Eight readings should not become eight presses

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Play the two invented presses. Compare counting every matching slot with consuming only the accepted canonical slot.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: 2 invented presses produced 16 events. All eight tracks contribute, multiplying each intended press by eight.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Invented aligned traces illustrate the documented DEL alias rule. They do not show the SP’s board wiring or scan timing.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: Two presses appear on each of eight alias tracks. Counting every track produces sixteen press events; consuming canonical slot 4 produces two.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: audio-stream (Mobile)

children.name: Demo title
children.text: Put the interrupt between the reads

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Change the read order. Keep the genuine-timeout and rollover cases to check what the correction must preserve.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: Elapsed: 255 ticks. Timeout. The interrupt supplied a newer last-block time than the already-read current clock. These are teaching values, not the R40 snapshot.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: An invented eight-bit timer with a 20-tick timeout threshold. Animation speed is not device timing.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: Racing reads produce (100 - 101) modulo 256 = 255. Ordered reads produce 3; a real gap produces 41; rollover produces 9. Only ages greater than 20 time out.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: pad-information (Desktop)

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Compare a direct renderer test with the screen that the owner actually used. Change the build, then follow the highlighted route.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: R1 current screen: stock drawing is reached, but the custom panel is missed.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Conceptual route diagram with invented sample data. R1’s route defect and the later wrong-build report were separate findings.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: R1: the direct renderer test reaches the custom panel, but the current screen reaches only the stock drawing. R2: the current screen draws stock content, then the custom panel. Neither route test identifies the installed build.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: bootloader-boundaries (Desktop)

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Commit or damage a fictional candidate record. Track which record is selected and which image remains confirmed.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: Record 2 is complete and selected. It still names A as confirmed and B only as a candidate. Metadata commitment does not establish a successful trial.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Fictional in-memory journal. This models neither a physical storage failure nor an independent recovery route.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: An incomplete candidate record is ignored. A complete candidate record can be selected while A remains confirmed. A damaged newest record falls back to the old valid record.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: pitch-correction (Mobile)

children.name: Demo title
children.text: An estimate is not a target note

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Move the estimated input frequency and change the allowed scale. Watch the target and correction ratio change.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: Estimate: MIDI 69.196. Target: A4, 440.00 Hz. Correction: -19.56 cents; ratio 0.988764. This chooses a note; it does not process sound.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: Musical selection from an invented pitch estimate. No microphone, detector, shifter or audio output runs here.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: An invented 445 Hz estimate is MIDI note 69.196. C major selects A4 at 440 Hz, giving a pitch ratio of 0.988764. This arithmetic does not establish corrected sound quality.

shape.name: OpenSP / Demo figures / Demo figure: first-animation (Desktop)

children.name: Demo title
children.text: The angle belongs to the widget

children.name: Demo prompt
children.text: Advance the callback at phase 63. Try another pad or external mode, then return to pad 1. Recreating the widget resets its state.

children.name: Demo result
children.text: Phase 63. The next callback advances to 0; recreating the widget resets it to 0. Callback count does not measure device frame rate.

children.name: Demo caption
children.text: An illustrative state model, independent of time. The separate R3 replay uses the preserved renderer frames; this diagram does not recreate them.

children.name: Demo fallback
children.text: A callback advances phase 63 to 0 on pad 1 outside external mode. Another pad or external mode holds the phase. Returning resumes it; recreating the widget initializes it to 0.
